title: Oscillation suppression playbook (personal lab notes)
content:
Objective:
Reduce sustained oscillations in throughput/latency observed on multi-tenant pools when ingress has correlated microbursts.

Hypothesis:
1) Deterministic batching + synchronous autoscale leads to positive feedback loops between load, batch formation, and scaling decisions.
2) Introducing small randomized jitter in batching timeouts and a lightweight exponential smoothing of per-worker load signal will damp oscillations without sacrificing steady-state throughput.

Experiment setup (local cluster replica):
- Fleet: 8 x A100-equivalent GPU containers, 2 workers per machine (simulated).
- Runtime: branch gh:runtime#4123 (local cpu/gpu harness with adaptive-batcher toggles).
- Workload generator: k6 script (bursting-arrival-v2.js) producing Zipfian client arrival, tunable burstiness.
- Measurement window: 45 minutes per run, 60s warmup ignored, metrics sampled at 5s resolution.
- Metrics captured: qps, p50/p95/p99 latencies (generation-only), in-flight batches, batch size distribution, eviction rate, autoscale events per minute.

Configs tested:
A) baseline: deterministic batch_timeout=12ms, no jitter, autoscaler: threshold-based (CPU/KV cache occupancy), smoothing alpha=0.0
B) jittered-batching: batch_timeout=12ms +- U(-3ms, +3ms), autoscaler same as A
C) jitter + smoothed-signal: batching as B, autoscaler smoothing alpha=0.15 (EWMA on observed qps per worker)
D) opportunistic-coalesce: batching uses tiered timeouts (short for small contexts), plus randomized backoff on scale-down (min cooldown 30s)

Quick commands used to run (notes):
- k6: k6 run --vus 200 --duration 10m bursting-arrival-v2.js --summary-export=runA.json
- telemetry: prometheus remote write to local grafana for scrape 5s
- postproc: python analyze_runs.py --inputs runA.json runB.json --metrics p99,throughput,osc_amp

Snapshot of raw observations (selected):
- Baseline (A): regular 2.5–3.2x oscillation amplitude in qps every ~120s. p95 spikes from 160ms -> 340ms at peaks.
- B (jittered): amplitude reduced ~35% measured on last 30m window; p95 improved at peaks by ~20ms median.
- C (jitter + smoothing): amplitude reduced ~62% relative to A; p99 tail improved and peak durations shorter. Throughput steady-state unchanged +/- 3%.
- D (opportunistic-coalesce): best p50 but occasional 1–2% throughput drop under extreme Zipfian hot keys due to longer coalesce windows.

Small numeric table (aggregated):
Config | mean qps | qps oscill_amp (coef) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | autoscale events/min
A      |  1200    | 0.34                 | 160     | 420     | 0.9
B      |  1196    | 0.22                 | 150     | 380     | 0.85
C      |  1201    | 0.13                 | 145     | 300     | 0.6
D      |  1175    | 0.11                 | 135     | 310     | 0.5

(Notes: oscill_amp computed as (qps_stddev / qps_mean) over 5s-sampled windows after warmup)

ASCII-ish sparkline of qps during a 10m window (representative):
A: ▁▂▇▂▁▇▂▁▇▂▇▂▁▇
C: ▁▁▂▁▁▂▁▁▁▁▁▂▁▁

Observational notes (free-form):
- Jittering batching timeouts introduces slight variability in batch sizes but breaks synchronization across workers. That alone helps a lot.
- EWMA on autoscaler input was helpful: smoothing removes high-frequency spikes that would otherwise trigger scale-out then rapid scale-in. Be careful with alpha tradeoffs — too large and reaction is sluggish.
- Opportunistic coalescing seems promising for p50 improvements (helps when many small contexts show up) but needs safe guards for hot-key scenarios (fallback shorter coalescing when per-context QPS exceeds x).
- The best combo for our current fleet: jittered batching + alpha~0.12–0.18 + min-scale-down-cooldown=25s.

Failure modes / gotchas encountered:
- If jitter range >> baseline batch_timeout, you start increasing p50 because many small requests wait longer. Keep jitter magnitude <= ~25% of base timeout.
- When load is very low, EWMA can hide real increases — ensure autoscaler also listens to short-window peak counters to avoid slow reaction during ramp-ups.
- Telemetry sampling at >10s windows masks micro-oscillations; keep >=5s sampling for these experiments.

Actionable next steps / TODOs:
- Run C variant across mixed-model fleet (gpt-like + embedder) to validate cross-model effects.
- Add 'hot-key detector' that forces coalesce window < 6ms if context qps > threshold.
- Perf-test with realistic client blend (mix of long tokens and short completions) — current k6 script biased to short generations.
- Draft a short "anti-oscillation" runbook for SRE runbook section: decision rules, safe defaults, rollbacks.

Personal notes to self:
- Keep experiment seeds logged (k6 has --seed) so runs are reproducible.
- Save raw traces for two full oscillation cycles for offline visualization.

References and quick links:
- GH:runtime#4123 (branch with jitter flags)
- JIRA INF-229 (task: autoscale smoothing + backoff)
- Slack thread C01AB2CDE (arch discussion 2025-10-12)

End of scratchpad.

-- Galen
conclusions: Small randomized jitter in batching timeouts plus moderate EWMA on autoscaler inputs consistently reduces throughput oscillation amplitude (~60% reduction in best runs) with negligible hit to steady-state throughput. Opportunistic coalescing helps p50 but must be gated by hot-key detection. Next: validate across heterogenous models and add safety heuristics before rolling to prod.
summary: Experiment journal showing that jittering batching timeouts + light smoothing of autoscale signals dampens oscillations caused by correlated microbursts. Practical parameter ranges and failure modes recorded.
notes: Keep this as living doc; may extract runbook bits into eng-serving-runtime/ops-runbooks later.
